issues.t: IMS bearing failure
issues.sym: Often no warning. Some cars show metal in the oil filter, an oil drip at the back of the engine, or a knocking or grinding noise from the rear of the engine.
issues.why: The intermediate shaft (IMS) bearing in these engines is sealed and can lose its grease and fail, wrecking the engine. The single-row bearing used around 2002-2005 has the highest failure rate. 2009 and newer engines have no IMS bearing.
issues.next: Ask for proof the bearing was upgraded. Many owners fit an upgraded bearing at the next clutch change. If you hear knocking from the back of the engine, stop driving.

issues.t: Cylinder bore scoring
issues.sym: Rising oil use, blue smoke, tapping or ticking from the engine, low oil level, and sooty tailpipes.
issues.why: The cylinder walls can get scratched by the pistons. PistonHeads says it hit about 1 in 20 pre-2009 engines, mostly the 3.4 S, and was almost unheard of on the 2.7.
issues.next: Have a specialist do a borescope (camera) check of the cylinders before buying or when oil use rises.

issues.t: Rear main seal oil leak
issues.sym: Oil drips where the engine meets the gearbox.
issues.why: The crankshaft rear seal leaks, often because the seal bore in the crankcase was machined slightly off-center. It mostly affected the 986, with fewer 987s.
issues.next: A small seep is not urgent. Because the gearbox has to come out, it's best done with a clutch or IMS job.

issues.t: Oil and coolant mixing on early engines
issues.sym: Milky oil on the dipstick, oil in the coolant tank, white exhaust smoke, or overheating.
issues.why: Early engines had casting weaknesses, and cracked cylinder heads or failed seals can let oil and coolant mix.
issues.next: Stop driving and have the fluids checked. If buying, check the dipstick and the oil and coolant fillers for any sign of mixing.

issues.t: Air-oil separator failure (blue smoke)
issues.sym: Blue or white smoke while driving or after start-up, high oil use, rough running or lean fuel codes.
issues.why: The air-oil separator, which vents crankcase gases, can fail internally and let oil be drawn into the intake. RepairPal lists this as the most reported Boxster problem.
issues.next: Check that the oil is not overfilled. Have the separator tested and replaced if needed.

issues.t: Water pump failure
issues.sym: Coolant leaks, a coolant smell, a whining noise, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: Water pumps on these cars may last only about 40,000 miles. The plastic impeller can crack and send debris through the system, and a failed pump can lead to head gasket damage.
issues.next: If the temperature climbs, stop and turn the engine off. Many owners replace the pump as preventive maintenance.

issues.t: Cracked coolant expansion tank
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping or coolant leaks into the trunk area.
issues.why: The plastic expansion tank on the 986 cracks with age.
issues.next: Have the tank pressure-tested and replaced before it leads to overheating.

issues.t: Misfire from cracked ignition coil packs
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough running, shaking or stuttering under power.
issues.why: The coil packs crack from heat and water splash.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read and replace the failed coil, often along with the spark plugs.

issues.t: Hesitation from failing mass air flow sensor
issues.sym: Stuttering or hesitation when you accelerate, and sometimes a check engine light.
issues.why: The mass air flow (MAF) sensor gets dirty or fails and sends wrong readings.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the sensor tested. Cleaning sometimes helps; otherwise replace it.

issues.t: Corroded front radiators and A/C condensers
issues.sym: Engine running warm, weak air conditioning, or leaks behind the front bumper. Leaves in the bumper vents.
issues.why: The radiators and condensers sit behind the bumper openings, where trapped leaves hold moisture and corrode them. They may last only six to eight years.
issues.next: Keep the bumper vents clear of debris. Replace a leaking radiator or condenser before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle at idle
issues.sym: A rattle at idle or at cold start.
issues.why: The timing chains and their tensioners and guide pads wear, especially with long oil-change intervals.
issues.next: Have it checked soon. Classic & Sports Car says worn cam chains need urgent replacement.

issues.t: Worn suspension bushings and joints
issues.sym: Knocking or creaking over bumps, groaning from the front when maneuvering, and odd tire wear.
issues.why: Suspension joints and rubber bushings, especially on the trailing arms and lower arms, often wear out by about 30,000-40,000 miles. Top mounts also wear.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected and the alignment checked after repairs.

issues.t: Broken coil springs
issues.sym: The car sits unevenly or makes clunks on rough roads.
issues.why: Coil spring breakage is very common on the 987.
issues.next: Have the springs inspected. A broken spring can damage a tire, so replace it promptly, ideally in pairs.

issues.t: Six-speed manual jumping out of second gear
issues.sym: The gearbox pops out of second gear under acceleration or deceleration.
issues.why: The six-speed manual can slip out of second because of wear in the selector detent.
issues.next: Have the gearbox inspected. The fix means stripping the gearbox and fitting a modified detent.

issues.t: Water behind seats from blocked roof drains
issues.sym: Wet carpet behind the seats, damp smells, or electrical faults.
issues.why: The drains for the soft top and hood area block with debris, so water collects behind the seats where a control unit sits.
issues.next: Clear the drains regularly. Water reaching the control unit can mean replacing it.

issues.t: Windows not dropping when doors open
issues.sym: The windows don't lower slightly when you open a door, or lower unexpectedly.
issues.why: A microswitch in the door handle that controls the window drop fails. RepairPal lists this as a common Boxster problem.
issues.next: Have the door handle switch replaced. Shutting the door with the window up can damage the seals or roof.

issues.t: Tiptronic shifter can leave Park without key (recall)
issues.sym: The shift lever can be moved out of Park with the key out.
issues.why: A misadjusted key-lock cable may let the shifter leave Park, which could let the car roll away.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and have a dealer inspect and adjust the cable for free.

issues.t: Cracked exhaust manifold
issues.sym: Engine sounds louder or harsher and feels sluggish.
issues.why: The exhaust manifolds can crack from heat.
issues.next: Have the exhaust inspected for leaks; exhaust leaks can also upset the oxygen sensors.

issues.t: Direct-injection carbon buildup and fuel pump wear
issues.sym: Gradual loss of smoothness or power, rough idle, or fuel-pressure check engine codes.
issues.why: Direct-injection engines can build up deposits on the intake valves and wear the high-pressure fuel pump. The base 2.7 on the 981 uses port injection and avoids this.
issues.next: Use good fuel and keep up with oil changes. Have codes read if the engine runs rough.

issues.t: Leaking PASM shock absorbers
issues.sym: A bouncy or harsh ride, a suspension warning, or oil on the shock body.
issues.why: The adaptive PASM dampers can leak.
issues.next: Have the shocks checked on a lift. Replace in pairs.

issues.t: Brake lights stay on from binding pedal bushes
issues.sym: Brake lights stay on and the PSM stability warning lights up. The brakes may run hot.
issues.why: Bushes in the brake pedal can bind, so the pedal doesn't fully return.
issues.next: Get it fixed soon, because the brakes can overheat if left. The fix needs a special tool.

issues.t: Front hood may not latch (recall)
issues.sym: The front lid may not stay securely closed.
issues.why: Hood lock parts built out of specification on cars made in mid-2014 may not latch properly.
issues.next: Have a dealer replace the front hood lock for free.

issues.t: Airbag control unit capacitor fault (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: A capacitor in the airbag control unit can fail, so the airbags may switch off or go off unexpectedly.
issues.next: Have a dealer update the software and replace the unit if needed. It's free.

issues.t: Seat side airbag may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning sign.
issues.why: The side airbag initiator in the seats of some 2017 718 Boxsters and Caymans may not fire in a crash.
issues.next: Have a dealer replace the side airbag modules for free.

issues.t: Trunk bracket could puncture fuel tank in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No sign in normal driving.
issues.why: A luggage compartment bracket could puncture the fuel tank in a certain type of collision. Porsche recalled over 14,000 718 Boxsters and Caymans in early 2019.
issues.next: Check with a dealer that the bracket fix has been done. It's free.

issues.t: Water pump or thermostat failure
issues.sym: Coolant loss, warning lights, overheating, or odd running in cold weather.
issues.why: On the 718, a failing water pump can drip coolant onto a vacuum hose. That can gum up vacuum valves, which then work on and off in the cold.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested and check the vacuum valves at the same time.

issues.t: Intermittent misfire that clears after restart
issues.sym: A slight misfire or rough running that goes away after switching off and on.
issues.why: PistonHeads says this is often linked to a weak 12-volt battery.
issues.next: Have the battery tested first. Watching battery voltage on the dash display can give early warning.

issues.t: Overheating from leaking transmission cooler valve
issues.sym: Temperature warning or the engine running hot.
issues.why: A leaking solenoid valve in the transmission cooling circuit can cause overheating.
issues.next: Stop if the temperature warning comes on and have the cooling system checked.

issues.t: Infotainment Bluetooth dropping or screen faults
issues.sym: Phones keep disconnecting, or the touchscreen stops working properly.
issues.why: The PCM infotainment unit can need recoding, and some touchscreens were replaced under warranty.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to recode the PCM; that usually fixes Bluetooth. Screen faults may need a new unit.

issues.t: GT4 connecting rods can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking from the bottom of the engine, stalling, loss of power, or oil leaks.
issues.why: GT4s built from late January to early March 2021 got connecting rods that were out of specification and can crack.
issues.next: Check with a dealer. Engines that had run were replaced; unrun engines got new rods and, in the US, a 10-year engine warranty.

issues.t: PDK may not lock in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The car may roll even when the shifter shows Park.
issues.why: A safety clip on the shift cable may be installed wrongly, so the transmission may not lock in Park.
issues.next: Always use the parking brake. Have a dealer replace the shift cable for free.

issues.t: Center-lock wheel bolt may fracture on GT4 RS and Spyder RS (recall)
issues.sym: A loose or vibrating wheel. Porsche said not to drive until repaired.
issues.why: On 2024 Cayman GT4 RS and Spyder RS models, the center-lock wheel bolt may crack, which could let a wheel come off.
issues.next: Don't drive the car until a dealer has checked and replaced faulty parts. It's free.
